claims.text: The initial Ti30Ni30Nb15Al15Cr10 alloy is predominantly single-phase after casting and homogenization.
The proposed alloy contains 30 at% Ti, 30 at% Ni, 15 at% Nb, 15 at% Al, and 10 at% Cr.
Aging near 800°C for 2 hours followed by rapid quenching can form nanoscale intermetallic precipitates in the proposed alloy.
The aging treatment can produce a fine and uniformly distributed precipitate population rather than coarse or brittle phases.
The aging-induced precipitates may include Ti2Ni or Laves phases.
Nanoscale intermetallic precipitates impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Nanoscale intermetallic precipitates impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion increases the alloy's resistance to plastic deformation and therefore its elevated-temperature yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding increase resistance to time-dependent creep deformation.
Optimized aging will increase elevated-temperature yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the cast-and-homogenized unaged baseline.
Optimized aging will improve creep resistance by approximately 20–30% relative to the cast-and-homogenized unaged baseline.
The predicted mechanical-property improvement applies during testing at 650–750°C.
Keeping the treatment within the thermal-stability limits of the phases can avoid coarse precipitates and embrittlement.
Precipitate coarsening may reduce ductility or toughness.
Precipitation hardening is a well-established strengthening mechanism.
